title: Suspect killed in robbery might have been serving conditional sentence
article: The robber killed by a Waterloo regional police officer this week may still have been serving a conditional sentence in connection with a holdup in Brantford a year ago.

Trevor Colin Graham, 26, was shot once in the chest Tuesday night after he was confronted by two uniformed officers responding to a robbery call at the Shoppers Drug Mart store in the Sunrise Shopping Centre in Kitchener.
He was fleeing with stolen prescription drugs when there was brief exchange with the officers in a vestibule at the front entrance of the store.
A civilian agency investigating the fatal shooting has not said if Graham was armed or provided details of the exchange with police.
In May, a man with the same name and age was sentenced to an eight-month conditional sentence after pleading guilty to offences related to a robbery at a Brantford coffee shop a year ago.
Already on probation at the time, he admitted being an accessory to the crime by assisting the robber.

Customers followed the culprit to a nearby apartment building, where he was let into a unit occupied by a man named Trevor Graham, then 25. A search of the apartment turned up clothes and brass knuckles used by the robber.
Initially charged with committing the robbery himself, he spent 160 days in jail before he was formally sentenced.

Identified as a Paris, Ont., man, he was given an eight-month conditional sentence, the first four months under house arrest, and a year on probation. The sentence stipulated that he live with his mother.

According to police, Graham resided in Kitchener at the time of the fatal shooting this week. In a profile posted on Facebook, a social networking website, a man giving the same name and date of birth as Graham listed interests including martial arts, ultimate fighting and working out.
He said he attended a private military boarding school called the Robert Land Academy in 1998.
Located near Welland, the school's website describes it as a facility for troubled but promising boys in grades six through 12.

More than two-thirds of its students, for instance, have been diagnosed with hyperactivity disorders. The profile also said the man attended public high schools in Hamilton and Dundas, near Hamilton, in 1999.
Photographs of a man identified as Trevor Colin Graham that were posted on the website show a stocky man with a shaved head.
Several young women listed as friends of Graham's on Facebook said they had chatted casually with the young man online, but knew little personal information about him.
One woman said she had met him in a Cambridge nightclub several years ago, another said she had met him through an online dating website.

Frank Phillips, spokesperson for the Special Investigations Unit, said local police have been co-operative during its investigation. The agency investigates all police incidents in which people are killed or seriously injured.
In this case, four officers have been formally designated as witnesses. The constable who shot Graham has been on the force for five years and remains on active, front-line duty.
The investigations unit expects its probe, meant to determine if there was any wrongdoing by police, to take four to six weeks.
The same Shoppers Drug Mart was held up by an armed, masked man Nov. 14, part of a recent rash of robberies on the west side of Kitchener.
The store reopened yesterday, and the only sign of Tuesday's shooting was a constable stationed by the cash registers.
Store employees were told not to talk about the incident, and deferred questions to their head office.
